## Caveat
The three attached images are anatomical illustrations and a clinic marketing banner — they contain **no quantitative data**. The numbers below are compiled from standard biomechanics literature (Novacheck 1998; Weyand 2000; Cavanagh;acceleration studies e.g. Nagahara 2014; Kugler & Janshen 2009). Use as rig-tuning starting points, not measured ground truth.

## Rig-Tuning Table

| Parameter | Walk | Jog | Max sprint | Initial accel (0–10 m) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Whole-body/trunk lean from vertical | ~3–5° | ~5–10° | ~15–20° (elite) | 35–45° first steps, decaying ~5°/step |
| Hip flexion contribution to lean | dominant (~60%) | dominant | dominant | dominant (~70%+) |
| Ankle (plantarflexor) contribution | ~20–25% | ~20% | ~10–15% | minimal |
| Spine/extra lumbar+thoracic flexion | ~1–3° | ~3–5° | ~5–8° (mostly thoracic) | 5–10° |
| Head/gaze counter-pitch (extension to keep gaze horizontal) | ~2–4° | ~4–6° | ~8–12° down-gaze acceptable; cervical extension ~5–8° | ~10–15° extension |
| Pelvis transverse rotation (total amplitude) | ~8–12° | ~10–15° | ~12–18° | ~15–20° |
| Shoulder-arm counter-rotation | ~10–15° | ~15–20° | ~25–40° (elbow fixed ~90°, arm swing ~±30–45° sagittal) | ~30–45° |
| Pelvis:shoulder counter-rotation ratio | ~1:1.2 | ~1:1.4 | ~1:2 | ~1:2 |

## Timing Rules (% of gait cycle)

| Phase | Walk | Run/Jog | Sprint | Accel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stance (contact) | ~60–62% | ~35–40% | ~22–30% | ~35–45% |
| Absorption (contact→mid-stance) | ~15–20% of cycle | ~12–15% | ~8–10% | ~12% |
| Drive/push-off | ~20–25% | ~15–20% | ~10–12% | ~20–25% |
| Flight | 0 (double support) | ~25–30% | ~35–40% | ~20–30% |
| Swing | ~38–40% | ~60–65% | ~70–78% | ~55–65% |
| Stride frequency | ~1.7–2 Hz | ~2.5–3 Hz | ~4.5–5 Hz (step) | 4–4.5 Hz early, rising |

## Lean-source rule of thumb (Kugler & Janshen)
Body lean (COM-to-ankle, not trunk) ≈ atan(a/g); trunk aligns to it primarily via **hip flexion**, with ankle contribution shrinking as speed rises. Rig: rotate root, distribute remaining lean hip-spine 4:1.

## Head/gaze rule
Cervical extension ≈ trunk lean angle minus ~2–5°; eyes stay locked on horizon or target. In sprint, allow slight gaze drop at foot contact (~1–2 m ahead).

**Key rig tuning knobs:** speed → lean ∝ acceleration not velocity; stance share shrinks from 60% to ~25%; shoulder counter-rotation grows faster than pelvis; hamstring images (biceps femoris) matter for the late-swing "hip extension + knee flexion" snap at ~70–80% of swing phase.
message.reasoning_content: Images are generic anatomy/gait marketing, not data sources. Provide literature-based numbers with caveat.
